title: Project Hertz attempt1
description: The task brief a fellow submits before starting the conversation: the attempt1/ folder at the root of the task repository, one plain-text file per field plus meta.txt for the short values (tools/paperwork.py maps them onto this shape). The older attempt1.json with this exact shape is still accepted.

task_code.description: The code shown in your task title. Must match this repository's name (hertz-<task_code>).

task_description.description: What you are trying to get done, for a reviewer who was not there. Copy this into the platform task form.

how_to_judge_completion.description: What a correct result looks like: commands to run, behaviour to check. Copy this into the platform task form.

reviewer_notes.description: Anything else that helps assess the outcome. May be empty. Copy this into the platform task form.

pr_url.description: Your codebase pull request in this task repository (into the codebase branch). The zip you mount comes from this branch.

commit_sha.description: Full 40-character commit on that pull request that the zip is taken from (normally its latest commit).

source.description: own = my own code I am allowed to share; oss_used = open-source repository I use or contribute to; oss_other = open-source repository I do not normally work with.

first_message.description: The first message you will send to the model, exactly. One paragraph is the target.

tier.description: t2 = contained feature (3-7 h); t3 = cross-cutting change (7-14 h); t4 = large refactor or extraction (15 h+).

watching_mode.description: live = you watch every response as it arrives; away = you let the model run long and check in. Affects how proactivity is judged.

mount_source.description: One line: what you will type when the platform asks where the mounted file came from (the real origin of the code; the client reads it). attempt1/mount_source.txt; absent in the older attempt1.json.
